tip.title: Find it, then look next door
tip.text: Order questions ask what happened BEFORE or AFTER an event. Here is the move: find the event from the question in the passage first. Then read the sentence right before it or right after it, depending on what the question asks. Signal words like FIRST, NEXT, and THEN help, but the sentence next door is the real proof. If the question says "right after Migs forgot his lines," find that line and read the very next sentence.

passage.title: Round One
passage.text:
Migs wrote raps on his phone every night. He was sixteen. He had never rapped in front of people.

At the fiesta there was a rap battle on the stage. The prize was two thousand pesos. Migs signed up.

First, the host called his name. Next, the beat started. Migs opened his mouth. Nothing came out. He forgot every line. A kid near the stage laughed.

Migs looked at the kid. Then he looked at the fishball stand and the tita selling cold drinks. He started to rap about them. The lines were not on his phone. They came out anyway. The crowd got loud.

He lost in the first round. The judges wanted clean rhymes. After the show, the host found him. "Next month, same stage," he said. Migs walked home with no prize. He did not stop smiling.

words.meaning: something you win in a contest
words.example: The prize for the quiz bee was a new tablet.

words.meaning: the people who decide who wins
words.example: The judges gave the dance crew a perfect score.

words.meaning: words that end with the same sound, like 'load' and 'road'
words.example: His song has rhymes in every line.

items.prompt: Where did Migs write his raps every night? (one word)
items.why: The first line says, "Migs wrote raps on his phone every night."

items.prompt: What happened FIRST when Migs was on stage?
items.why: The signal word tells you: "First, the host called his name."

items.prompt: What happened right AFTER Migs forgot every line?
choices: A kid near the stage laughed.
items.why: "He forgot every line. A kid near the stage laughed." The laugh comes right after.

choices: Migs making up new lines about the fiesta
items.why: The paragraph shows Migs looking around and rapping about what he sees. The tita and the crowd are details inside that.

items.prompt: "The judges wanted clean rhymes." What does "clean" mean here?
items.why: Migs made up his lines on the spot and lost, so the judges wanted rhymes with no mistakes.

items.prompt: Put the events in the order they happened.
steps: Migs signed up for the rap battle.
He rapped about the fishball stand and the tita.
He lost in the first round.
The host told him to come back next month.
items.why: The story goes: sign up, freeze on stage, rap about the crowd, lose, then the host's offer after the show.

items.prompt: Which title fits the whole passage best?
items.why: The whole story is about Migs finding a way to rap in front of people. The prize and the kid are small parts.

items.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?
choices: A boy who freezes in a rap battle but finds a new way to rap
A fiesta with many food stands
Judges who pick the best rhymes
A host who runs a stage
items.why: Topic: Migs at the rap battle. The point: he froze, then rapped his own way and got asked back. That is the whole story.

items.prompt: What was the prize for the rap battle?
What did the host say to Migs after the show?
items.why: "After the show, the host found him. 'Next month, same stage,' he said."
